Supporting foundation: Free coherent monad modules and their augmented free resolution. Supporting lemma: Underlying equivalences and operadic colimits of coherent modules. Supporting step: Colimits of sections from preserved local fiber cocones. Fiber-to-relative-colimit criterion used before assembling the chosen cocones. Mapping-space fiber over one edge used in the local fiber criterion's comparison with the edge pullback.

title: Mapping-space fibers over an edge are mapping spaces in the edge pullback
statement:
Use simplicial sets, quasicategories, functor simplicial sets $\operatorname{Fun}(K,-)$, constant-diagram maps $\Delta_K$, coherent composition, right-pinched mapping spaces, Kan complexes, homotopy fibers and weak homotopy equivalences as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and inner fibrations as in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. A Kan fibration is a simplicial map with the right lifting property against every horn inclusion $\Lambda_k^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$, $n\geq1$, $0\leq k\leq n$. Let $p:E\to B$ be an inner fibration between quasicategories, and let $f:b\to s$ be an edge of $B$ (possibly degenerate). Let $E_f=E\times_{B,f}\Delta^1$ be the degreewise pullback, with projections $j:E_f\to E$ and $p_f:E_f\to\Delta^1$. Its fibers over $0$ and $1$ are $E_b=E\times_B\{b\}$ and $E_s=E\times_B\{s\}$, and an object $y$ of one of them is written $(y,0)$, respectively $(y,1)$, in $E_f$. Let $K$ be a small simplicial set, possibly empty, and let $A:K\to E_b$ and $Z:K\to E_s$ be diagrams. Write $p_K:\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,B)$ for postcomposition with $p$. Then:

(1) $p_K$ is an inner fibration between quasicategories, $E_f$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E_f)$ are quasicategories, and $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E_f)=\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)\times_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,B)}\operatorname{Fun}(K,\Delta^1)$ degreewise.

(2) $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\Delta^1)}(\Delta_K0,\Delta_K1)$ has exactly one simplex in each degree. Postcomposition with $f$ carries it to the constant vertex $\Delta_Kf$ of $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,B)}(\Delta_Kb,\Delta_Ks)$ and its degeneracies.

(3) The map $\pi:\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)}(A,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,B)}(\Delta_Kb,\Delta_Ks)$ induced by $p_K$ is a Kan fibration between Kan complexes. Postcomposition with $j$ is an isomorphism of simplicial sets from $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,E_f)}((A,0),(Z,1))$ onto the strict fiber $\pi^{-1}(\Delta_Kf)$. Followed by the constant-path inclusion of that strict fiber into $\operatorname{hofib}_{\Delta_Kf}(\pi)$, it gives a weak homotopy equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,E_f)}((A,0),(Z,1))\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\operatorname{hofib}_{\Delta_Kf}\bigl(\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)}(A,Z)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,B)}(\Delta_Kb,\Delta_Ks)\bigr).$$

(4) These equivalences are induced by the simplicial map $j$, and they are natural. They commute with restriction along any simplicial map $L\to K$ and with the constant-diagram maps $\Delta_K$. They also commute with coherent precomposition by an edge of $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E_b)$ and with coherent postcomposition by an edge of $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E_s)$, when the composite is formed in $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E_f)$ and its image under $j$ is taken as the composite in $\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)$. Such an image lies over the degenerate composite with $\Delta_Kf$ in $\operatorname{Fun}(K,B)$.

For $K=\Delta^0$ this says that, for $x\in E_b$ and $z\in E_s$, $\operatorname{Map}_E(x,z)\to\operatorname{Map}_B(b,s)$ is a Kan fibration whose fiber over $f$ is $\operatorname{Map}_{E_f}((x,0),(z,1))$, equivalent to the homotopy fiber over $f$. No cocartesian or cartesian edge of $p$ is assumed.
